key_insight: Token-level shifts from privileged self-distillation are driven more by counterfactual sensitivity than by true answer-aligned learning value, so credit should be reallocated away from highly sensitive tokens.
engineering_relevance: CSCR is a simple drop-in modification to GRPO that preserves verifier-determined direction while improving long-CoT reasoning performance on mathematical benchmarks.
method: Re-score each sampled trajectory under two counterfactual outcomes: correct vs. incorrect.
Measure which tokens change most and downweight highly sensitive, easily substitutable tokens.
Renormalize token-level advantages to keep the original credit budget and update direction.
evidence_signal: On long-CoT mathematical reasoning benchmarks, CSCR consistently beats the GRPO baseline with the same number of policy updates, and ablations show moderate downweighting works best.
watch_item: Over-modulating token credit can destabilize optimization, so the sensitivity downweighting must be kept moderate.
paper_title: Not All Tokens Deserve Equal Credit: Counterfactual Sensitivity Credit Reallocation for Long-CoT Reasoning
